problem_statement: Existing social simulations frequently treat interventions as exogenous labels and do not close the source-intervention, crowd-response and public-signal feedback loop, limiting causal auditability and trajectory fidelity.

rationale.innovation: Execute IntervenSim as an endogenous multi-round feedback loop with explicit group state, interventions, public signals and reproducible artifacts.
reasoning_chain: Public reactions change after each source intervention and those reactions influence the next intervention.
A static rollout cannot represent this bidirectional dependence.
IntervenSim records source actions, group updates and population-weighted public signals on every round.
Held-out event trajectories can test whether the closed loop improves prediction and intervention-response accuracy over static rollouts.
rationale.falsifiable_hypothesis: On held-out events, the closed IntervenSim feedback loop will reduce normalized trajectory RMSE and intervention-response error versus a no-feedback simulation.

technical_details.model_runtime: Qwen open-source-family model through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio (Bailian) API
reproducibility_controls: immutable source SHA-256 and transformation lineage
fixed random seeds, cutoff timestamps and environment versions
agent execution trace plus redacted Qwen/Bailian call receipt
human approval recorded separately from automatic validation

source.name: IntervenSim social-event benchmark (SNB)
source.description: Forty-two real 2024 online events used by the IntervenSim social-simulation track, with engagement fields and seven-point historical traffic trajectories.
source.provenance: The benchmark is distributed by the GA-S3 authors and reused here only as audited historical input to IntervenSim; the bundled copy is byte-identical to the project display archive.
source.usage_rights: Publicly distributed research benchmark; retain attribution and complete the organizer/institutional data-use review before external redistribution.
historical_features: view, like, share and comment counts
source.pii_assessment: Aggregate event and engagement fields only; no direct personal identifiers are used by the research planner.
source.redistribution_scope: Derived metrics and hashes may be submitted; redistribution of the bundled source requires the original terms and attribution review.
source.verification_method: Record-count and SHA-256 verification against the project display archive plus repository/source metadata review.

target.name: Prospective social-event intervention-response panel
target.collection_scope: At least 30 newly observed public social events recorded at fixed intervals before and after source-side interventions.
target.unit_of_analysis: event x time window x de-identified population group
planned_features: timestamped views, likes, comments, shares and follows
intervention type, text, issuer, timestamp and objective
de-identified group attributes and population weights
group state, exposure controls, event category and exogenous shocks
IntervenSim round id, public signal and next-intervention linkage
target.sampling_strategy: Stratify by event category and intervention type; freeze a chronological event-level split before evaluation.
target.consent_and_privacy: Collect only lawfully accessible or consented records; remove direct identifiers, minimize retained text and complete ethics/data-protection review before collection.
quality_controls: pre-register inclusion/exclusion rules and primary metrics
version data, code, prompts, Qwen model id and random seeds
retain immutable raw-data hashes and transformation lineage
deduplicate reposts without deleting raw audit records

paper_title: Closing the Intervention-Response Loop in Auditable Multi-Agent Social Simulation

paper_abstract.background: Social-event simulators rarely model how crowd response changes subsequent source intervention.
paper_abstract.methods: We implement an IntervenSim feedback loop with Qwen/Bailian source and crowd agents, population-weighted signals, explicit intervention traces and held-out trajectory evaluation.
paper_abstract.expected_results: We expect lower trajectory and intervention-response error than persistence and no-feedback baselines while retaining a complete execution audit.

methods.name: Event audit
methods.procedure: Select a provenance-audited event and freeze its historical comparison trajectory.

methods.name: Group hierarchy
methods.procedure: Construct population groups and initial attitudes with no personally identifiable records.

methods.name: Feedback-loop execution
methods.procedure: Alternate source intervention, concurrent crowd updates and public-signal aggregation.

methods.name: Trajectory evaluation
methods.procedure: Compare normalized predicted traffic with frozen historical traffic and run feedback ablations.

baselines.name: Persistence
baselines.description: Repeat the most recent observed state.

baselines.name: No source feedback
baselines.description: Keep source intervention fixed throughout the rollout.

baselines.name: Deterministic update
baselines.description: Use rule-based group transitions without Qwen reasoning.

metrics.name: Spearman rho
metrics.definition: Rank correlation of predicted and observed trajectories.

metrics.name: Intervention-response error
metrics.definition: Error in change following an intervention.

experiments.split_strategy: Hold out entire events; tune only on earlier events and preserve event-level temporal order.
experiments.decision_rule: Support only if the feedback loop lowers normalized RMSE and intervention-response error on the preregistered held-out event set.

results.interpretation: The current IntervenSim source-intervention, crowd-update and public-signal loop executed and emitted frontend-aligned trajectories. This establishes engineering feasibility for one event only.
results.claim_scope: Actual one-event simulation execution; no cross-event confirmatory claim.
